criteria.evidence: Every section is substantive: What it does (four bullets, e.g. "It lists each needed type with its one-line meaning and says which are missing. After the product owner's typed yes, it makes each missing type and records what it made."), Inputs / Outputs (each of the six types with its meaning; brief, made types, mapping, record), Rules & behavior (no, partial yes, make fails, earlier mapping), nine Given/When/Then criteria, Out of scope naming owners, and an Agent intent (ICE) with Goal, Limit, Fails if, Context and Checked by.

"Nothing is made in the tracker before the product owner's typed yes. A tracker is an outside system, and a new type there is seen by the whole team."; "so adding a tracker adds one adapter and changes no play"; "because a yes to one type is not a yes to another"; "because one failure says nothing about them"; "because the plays already file work by it".

Discrete bullets throughout; the feature states the function's behavior ("Runs as part of `initialize`. It reads which tracker the project uses..."), never a user story; acceptance is Given/When/Then, e.g. "Given Epic and Spike are missing, when the product owner types yes for Epic only, then only Epic is made, and the brief and the record name Spike as still missing."

Parent capability gives one line: "Set up the tracker's work-item types (fn-881): finds the tracker the project uses and the types it has, makes each missing type after a typed yes, and records a stand-in where a type cannot be made." The feature adds the six types with meanings, the mapping and record shapes, the no / partial-yes / make-failed / earlier-mapping branches, and nine testable criteria.

"When a tracker cannot make a type, initialize says so in plain words, names the type it uses in its place, and records that in the mapping." and "Given a tracker that cannot make a type, when initialize runs, then it says so in plain words, names the stand-in type, and the mapping holds that stand-in." versus "When a mapping already exists from an earlier run, initialize keeps it ... and changes it only on a new typed yes"; also "Jira and Linear come through the same adapter".
criteria.fix: Add a rule in Rules & behavior that says who picks a stand-in and how (for example: initialize proposes the closest existing tracker type, such as a label or the plain Issue type, shows it in the brief, and writes it to the mapping only on the product owner's typed yes), and add that yes to the matching acceptance criterion, so a reader can tell whether a first stand-in needs the same yes that a later change to the mapping needs. Say in one line how initialize tells "the tracker cannot make this type" (gets a stand-in) apart from "making it failed" (left unmapped). Explain "the adapter" in one line the first time it appears: the one piece that talks to a given tracker, so the plays never call a tracker directly.
